text:
Predicates:
SpillsFood(x) ::: x spills a lot of food on his clothing.
Tidy(x) ::: x is notably tidy.
ClumsyFoodie(x) ::: x is a clumsy foodie who goes out frequently to find new food restaurants to try.
Clean(x) ::: x is cleanly.
ValuablesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) ::: x values order and spotlessness.
FamilyPrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) ::: x's family prioritizes order and spotlessness.
Peter ::: Peter.
Premises:
∀x (SpillsFood(x) → ¬Tidy(x)) ::: If people spill a lot of food on their clothing, then they are not notably tidy.
∀x (ClumsyFoodie(x) → SpillsFood(x)) ::: All clumsy foodies who go out frequently to find new food restaurants to try are people who spill a lot of food on their clothing.
∀x (Tidy(x) → Clean(x)) ::: If people are cleanly, then they are notably tidy.
∀x (ValuablesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) → Clean(x)) ::: If people value order and spotlessness, then they are cleanly.
∀x (FamilyPrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) → ValuablesOrderAndSpotlessness(x)) ::: All people whose families prioritize order and spotlessness themselves value order and spotlessness.
(SpillsFood(peter) ∧ Tidy(peter)) ∨ (¬SpillsFood(peter) ∧ ¬Tidy(peter)) ::: Peter is either a person who spills a lot of food on his clothing and is cleanly, or a person who does not spill a lot of food on his clothing and is not cleanly.
Conclusion:
((ClumsyFoodie(peter) ∧ FamilyPrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(peter)) ∨ (¬ClumsyFoodie(peter) ∧ ¬FamilyPrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(peter))) ::: Peter is either both a clumsy foodie who goes out frequently to find new food restaurants to try and is someone whose family prioritizes order and spotlessness, or he neither is a clumsy foodie who goes out frequently to find new food restaurants to try nor does his family prioritize order and spotlessness.
